O R D E R
PER HON’BLE MR. VIRENDER BHAT, JUDICIAL MEMBER
IA No.1789 OF 2025 IN APPEAL No.350 OF 2025 &
IA No.1936 OF 2025 IN APPEAL No.57 OF 2026
(For interim relief)
1. By way of these applications, the appellants have sought stay of the
order dated 31.10.2025 passed by the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory
Commission (in short “the Commission”) in case no.03/2025, which has
been assailed in these two appeals.
2. It appears that the 2nd respondent Maharashtra State Load
Despatch Centre (in short “MSLDC”) had, under the MERC (Deviation
Settlement Mechanism and Related Matters) Regulations, 2019, prepared
a procedure for “Apportionment of Legacy Dues Charges Bills of WRLDC
by MSLDC to State Entities”. Some of the state entities raised objections
to the said procedure and did not pay the bills raised in terms thereof.
Accordingly, the 2nd respondent approached the Commission by way of a
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 10 of 21

petition bearing case no.3/2025 for removal of difficulty under DSM
Regulations, 2019 and seeking approval of the methodology for
apportionment of Legacy Charges to be paid by Western Regional Load
Despatch Centre (WRLDC) among the State Entities.
3. The petition has been disposed of by the Commission vide the
impugned order dated 31.10.2025 thereby approving the methodology
proposed by the 2nd respondent MSLDC. The Commission has held that
intra-state thermal power generators also are liable to share burden of
Legacy Charges and directed them to deposit the Legacy dues within a
period of one month from the date of the order.
4. In terms of the impugned order, the 2nd respondent MSLDC raised
invoices dated 04.11.2025 and 06.11.2025 upon the appellants which own
and operate thermal power stations in the State of Maharashtra.
5. Feeling aggrieved, these two appeals have been filed by two power
generators operating in the State of Maharashtra claiming following
reliefs: -
Appeal No.350 of 2025:
“a) Set aside the impugned order dated 31.10.2025
passed by the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 11 of 21

Commission in Case No. 3 of 2025, to the extent that it
allows recovery of legacy dues from the injecting entities
such as the Appellants herein, in terms as stated in the
present Appeal;
b) Consequently, quash the letters cum invoices dated
20:01.2025, 04.11.2025 and 06.11.2025 raised by
MSLDC, to the extent of Legacy Dues and Delayed
Payment Surcharge imposed upon the Appellants; and
c) Pass any order and/ or any such orders as this Hon'ble
Tribunal may deem appropriate.”
Appeal No.57 of 2026:
“A. Set aside the Impugned Order dated 31.10.2025
passed by Respondent No. 1, MERC in Case no. 3 of
2025, approving the levy and directing the appellant to pay
Regional Pool Legacy Charges; and
B. Direct the Respondent no. 2/MSLDC to refund the
entire amount paid by the Appellant under protest as
Regional Pool Legacy Charges for the period 16.09.2023
to 15.09.2024, of Rs.3,57,47,088.08/-along with interest
@ 18% p.a.; and
C. Direct the Respondent no. 2/MSLDC to refund the
entire amount paid by the Appellant under protest as
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 12 of 21

Regional Pool Charges demand for the period 16.09.2024
to 02.11.2025 of Rs. 22,99,760/- along with interest @
18% p.a.; and
D. Restrain the Respondent no. 2/MSLDC from raising
any further demands on the Appellant, based on the
statements and demands of NLDC/WRLDC made against
Respondent no. 2, in respect of deficits in the Regional
Pool; and/or
E. Pass any other order(s) as the Hon’ble Tribunal may
deem just, fit and proper.”
6. As already noted hereinabove, in the applications at hand the
appellants have prayed for stay of the impugned order as well as the
consequential demands raised by the 2nd respondent.
7. It appears that the appellant in appeal no.57 of 2026 has paid certain
amount to the 2nd respondent MSLDC as Regional Pool Legacy Charges
under protest, and therefore, prayer has been made in the said appeal for
direction to the 2nd respondent MSLDC to refund the entire amount, so
paid under protest by the appellant, to the appellant along with interest.
However, in so far as the prayer made in the interim application i.e. IA
No.1936/2025 in the said appeal is concerned, the same is limited to the
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 13 of 21

stay of the operation of impugned order of the Commission as well as
restraining the 2nd respondent MSLDC from making further demands/bills
based on the statements published by NLDC from time to time in
pursuance to the impugned order of the Commission.
8. We may note here that in appeal no.350 of 2025 there are total 31
respondents whereas in appeal no.57 of 2026 there are only two
respondents. Maharashtra State Load Despatch Center (MSLDC) is
respondent no.2 in both the appeal, whereas Maharashtra Electricity
Regulatory Commission is respondent no.1 in both the appeals.
9. We have heard Shri Amit Kapur, learned counsel for the
appellant/applicant, Mr. B.P. Patil, learned senior counsel appearing for
respondent no.3 as well as learned counsels appearing for respondent
nos.1, 2, 4 and 18. Written submissions filed by the learned counsels
have been perused.
10. Lengthy and elaborate arguments were advanced by the learned
counsels for the parties. Arguments on behalf of the appellants being that
the DSM Regulations, 2019 do not contemplate recovery of Legacy DSM
dues from the injecting entities i.e. the power generators thereby
reinforcing the settled principle that DSM dues deficits are to be borne
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 14 of 21

only by drawee entities responsible for grid drawl imbalances and
therefore, the impugned order being contrary to the Regulations cannot
be given effect to.
11. Respondent no.18 supports the appellants in saying that the
impugned order is directly in violation of the DSM Regulations, 2019.
12. The application is vehemently resisted by respondent nos.1 & 2 in
both the appeals besides by respondent nos.3 & 4 in appeal no.350 of
2025. It is submitted that impugned order has been passed by the
Commission after due and detailed consideration of the applicable
regulatory framework under the DSM Regulations, 2019 and has correctly
come to the conclusion that payments towards the Regional Deviation and
Ancillary Services Pool Account are mandatorily routed through the Intra-
State DSM Pool. It is submitted that Intra-State generating units are also
responsible and accountable for their respective deviations based on
“causer pays’ principle followed in the DSM Regulations and thus, they
are also required to pay the DSM Charges in the Intra-State DSM Pool for
their deviations. It is further argued that the Commission has not created
a new category of tariff nor has it imposed any retrospective liability. The
Commission has merely exercised powers available under the existing
framework including Regulation 19 to remove operational difficulties and
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 15 of 21

has thus, issued appropriate directions to make the regulatory framework
workable. Learned counsels for these respondents vociferously argued
that no case for stay of the impugned order or the consequential demands
raised by 2nd respondent, has been made out and the application
deserves outright dismissal.
13. We have referred to the rival submissions of the learned counsels
for the parties in nutshell only and do not find it necessary to record and
discuss each and every argument advanced by them as we feel inclined
to allow the application at hand in view of the following reasons.
14. We note that in Paragraph no.27 of the impugned order the
Commission has taken note of the pendency of the two Writ Petitions i.e.
WP(C) No. 5392 of 2025 and WP(C) No.12647 of 2025 filed by Punjab
State Power Corporation Limited and North Bihar Power Distribution
Company Limited respectively in the Hon’ble Delhi High Court wherein the
order passed by Central Electricity Regulatory Commission regarding
retrospective recovery of Legacy Charges has been challenged. We find
it pertinent to extract hereunder Paragraph Nos.27, 28 and 29 of the
impugned order in this context: -
“27 In this context, the Commission notes that Writ
Petition (WP(C) No. 5392 of 2025) filed by Punjab State
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 16 of 21

Power Corporation Limited and Writ Petition (WP(C) No.
12647 of 2025) filed by North Bihar Power Distribution
Company Limited challenging the Order passed by the
CERC regarding the retrospective recovery of these
Legacy Charges are pending before the Hon’ble Delhi
High Court. These Writ Petitions were listed for hearing
before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court on 23 September
2025, and the next hearing in these Writ Petitions is
scheduled on 9 December 2025.
28 Thus, the legality of these Legacy Charges is being
examined by the Hon’ble Delhi High Court, and the
matter is sub-judice before the Hon’ble High Court.
Hence, it would not be appropriate for this
Commission to deal with the legal issues raised by
the Respondents regarding CERC Order/NLDC
Procedure in present proceeding.
29 Also, although the Wirt Petitions are pending
before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court, from
submissions of the Respondents, it is observed that
there is no stay to the levy of Legacy Charges directed
through the CERC Order and the NLDC procedure.
Hence, the Commission is of the view that the CERC
Order and the NLDC procedure have to be followed by
all concerned DICs.”
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 17 of 21

15. From these observations of the Commission in Paragraph No.29 of
the impugned order, it is evident that the Commission found it justified to
continue the proceedings of the Commission and to pass final order as no
stay with regards to levy of Legacy Charges had been passed by the
Hon'ble Delhi High Court in these two Writ Petitions. This is indicative of
the fact that in case any stay had been granted by the Hon'ble Delhi High
Court in these two Writ Petitions as regards to the levy of Legacy Charges,
the Commission may not have continued the proceedings of the petition
and may not have passed the final order.
16. Even in the concluding observations, the Commission has directed
the MSLDC to monitor the status of these two writ petitions before the
Hon’ble Delhi High Court and to take appropriate steps after any decision
is rendered by Hon’ble Delhi High Court in the writ petitions. The relevant
portion of the impugned order is extracted hereinbelow: -
“ORDER
…………………………………………………………………
…………………………………………………………………
4. MSLDC is directed to monitor the status of the Writ
Petitions filed before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court,
challenging the Legacy Charges, and take appropriate
steps after the Hon’ble Delhi High Court decides the Writ
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 18 of 21

Petition (WP (C) No.5392 of 2025) (WP (C) No.12647 of
2025)”
17. During the course of arguments, it has been conveyed to us that
vide order dated 09.12.2025 passed in these two Writ Petitions, the
Hon’ble Delhi High Court has stayed the deficit recovery statement issued
for levy of Legacy dues. Copy of the said order dated 09.12.2025 was
produced which has been perused. The operative portion of the said order
is extracted hereinbelow: -
“3. In the meanwhile, having regard to the various interim
orders passed by various High Courts, where similar
issues have been raised, we provide that there shall be
stay on the Deficit Recovery Statement issued by the
respondent no.2 on 17.09.2025, 31.10.2025, 14.11.2025
and 28.11.2025, till the next date of listing.”
18. Moreover, it has also been brought to our notice on behalf of the
appellant that various other High Courts also have stayed the levy of
Legacy Charges. Hon’ble Kerala High Court vide order dated 10.04.2025
in WPC No. 13482 of 2025, titled as KSEB v. CERC & Ors, granted an
interim protection of 2 months to KSEB. This protection has since
continued and is in force. Hon'ble Madras High Court by order dated
13.06.2025 passed in WP No. 20912 of 2025, titled as TNPDCL v. Ministry
of Power, Union of India & Ors., granted interim stay on the demand
_________________________________________________________________________________
IA No.1789/2025 in Appeal No.350 of 2025 &
IA No.1936/2025 in Appeal No.57 of 2026 Page 19 of 21

notices issued by the Regional SLDC upon the State Discom. Hon'ble
Andhra Pradesh High Court by order dated 21.07.2025 passed in Writ
Petition No. 18517 of 2025, titled as Central Power Distribution
Corporation Ltd v. UOI & Ors., suspended (for the interim period) the
operation of order dated 08.01.2025 passed by Ld. CERC in Petition No.
1/SM/2025 and demand notices issued by the Regional SLDC upon the
Petitioner. The said interim protection was extended by the Hon'ble High
Court vide orders dated 19.08.2025 and 14.10.2025. Hon'ble Telangana
High Court by order dated 24.07.2025 passed in WP No. 19729 of 2025,
titled as Southern Power Distribution Company of Telangana Limited v.
CERC & Ors., directed NLDC and the Regional SLDC not to take any
coercive measures for recovery of legacy dues pertaining to the period
prior to 16.09.2024, against the Petitioner, till the next date of hearing.
19. Therefore, once the levy of Legacy Charges has been challenged
by various entities by way of writ petitions filed in various High Courts, as
